newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA ANNOUNCE LUCRATIVE NEW CONTRACT FOR LITTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA ANNOUNCE LUCRATIVE NEW CONTRACT FOR LITTLE.

text.p: Aston Villa manager Brian Little has signed a new five-year contract which will keep him at Villa Park until 2002, the English premier league club said on Friday.

Villa chairman Doug Ellis said Little agreed the deal, reportedly worth two million pounds ($3.4 million), on New Year's Day -- a week before speculation linked him to the vacant manager's post at Newcastle.

"We talked about the contract in the summer," Ellis said. "I told Brian then to wait until the New Year when we would sort something out. We presented the contract to him on January 1 and he signed it immediately.
"When there was all the panic and speculation about him going to Newcastle, I knew that he wasn't going there because he had already signed the new contract. I was quietly smiling."
A Newcastle supporter as a child, Little had been seen as a candidate to take over from Kevin Keegan, who resigned as manager at St James's Park on Wednesday.
But within hours of Keegan's resignation he pledged himself to Villa, whom he guided to the English League Cup and fourth place in the championship last season.
He still had 2-1/2 years left on his existing contract, which is now annulled by the new deal.

"I came here wanting to be successful and have the opportunity to be here for some time," said Little, who took over from Ron Atkinson in November 1994. "I would like to be here for even more than five years but that depends on if we are successful."
His first match in charge since the deal was announced will be at Villa Park on Saturday -- against Newcastle.
Little, who has faced a number of dressing-room rebellions from discontented players this season, acknowledged his Yugoslav international Sasa Curcic was still unsettled at the club.

Last weekend Curcic described his four million pounds ($6.7 million) move from Bolton as "the biggest mistake of my life" and said he wanted to leave Villa. He subsequently sent a letter of apology to Little but has not fully resolved the issue.

"He's said nothing else other than the apology and there seems to be a problem," Little said. "He seems to have something on his mind. There definitely seems to have been something which has aggravated him.
"I've said to him that when we get this week out of the way then we'll sit down and try and iron out what is chewing away at him."
